title: Donkey Kong Country

masks.why: Cranky's intro and the level-name screens are drawn for 256 columns on a 32-tile map that would repeat (BG1 map at $7C00)

issues: The game draws new columns of the level only 8 to 16 pixels ahead of the SNES edge: on the side Donkey Kong runs towards, the side columns beyond that show old tiles (a visible seam) until he gets there.
Behind him the sides are right: the game keeps the columns it drew.
Cranky's intro and the level-name screens are shown with black sides.
Enemies appear near the SNES edge (the game creates them as they come near).
No flicker: in the 4,400 frames checked the game never drew more sprites on a line than a SNES shows, so it changed nothing; it changes only lines over the limits.
Fast CPU ran the 4,400 frames checked, from power-on and switched on later; the game's timing changes.

verified.how: Workshop --wms-test (E6), 4,400 frames of a pad script (intro, Jungle Hijinxs) in lockstep with the SNES console: widescreen's centre 256 columns identical to the SNES picture every frame, STAT77 and the sound identical, switched off frame-identical; no flicker changes only lines over the SNES's limits; better sound changes only the sound.
